title: A hand kick-back into FIXME writes the ticket's fixme list
intention: Every crossing back into FIXME that carries a ticket writes that ticket's fixme list from its missing=[...], so the FIXME gate reads a list each door into FIXME writes.
why: Measured 2026-10-29 on 7a31059daa23: a hand kick-back through emit journaled missing at history seq 63 and wrote no fixme list (only harbor_master clearance writes it), so the BUILDME re-crossing refused FixmeGateRed until the list was copied onto the ticket by hand.
traces_to: Law 4 (the FIXME gate is physics; a door into FIXME that skips its list makes the gate refuse for a reason nobody wrote); Law 7 (the record of truth carries what the crossing said)
how: In cairn/tools/base/transitions.emit, when the target is a repair summons entered as a back-edge with missing=[...] and the crossing carries a ticket, write the ticket's fixme list as [{n: i, kind: 'hand_kickback', missing: m}] numbered from 1, through the artifact door, in the same act as the journal entry; the clearance path keeps writing its own list and emit does not write twice when clearance already has.
falsifier: Done when: a hand emit(..., 'FIXME', missing=['a','b'], ticket=<id>) over a scratch commons leaves the ticket with fixme [{n:1,...'a'},{n:2,...'b'}], and a clearance kick-back still writes exactly one list. Wrong intent if the hand kick-back is meant to be impossible, i.e. every kick-back must go through clearance.

decisions.text: D1 (the /sorted builder_check): A Haiku builder would ask: which door writes the ticket (cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write, verb cast); what kind string a hand entry carries ('hand_kickback'); how to find the ticket (the existing ticket locator base uses for the entry gate); what to do when clearance already wrote the list (leave it). The ticket's how answers each.

EXISTS (measured 2026-10-30): cairn/tools/base/transitions.py defines emit(workflow_str, target, *, history_path, state_path, node_class_root, **journal_extra) and already imports 'from cairn.tools.base import ticket_file as _tf'; cairn/tools/base/ticket_file.py defines find_ticket(name, tickets_dir=None) (reads _TICKETS at call time), read_ticket(path) and rewrite_ticket(plan, doc, *, why, verb). emit resolves the crossing's ticket (journal_extra['ticket']) with _tf.find_ticket — the locator the FIXME gate reads with — and writes through _tf.read_ticket + _tf.rewrite_ticket(verb='cast'); a name that does not resolve is said on stderr and nothing is written

owning_intention is cairn/tools/base/intention+why.json, the charter beside the build's code address (transitions.py), which the PROVED owner-gate reads for gated_by; CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md is a .md the gate cannot parse and stays the intention the ticket serves. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

BUILT (commit 7f4c9576): cairn/tools/base/transitions.py emit takes keyword-only write_fixme=True; on a back-edge into a repair summons whose crossing names a ticket it writes fixme [{n, kind: hand_kickback, missing}] after the journal via _tf.rewrite_ticket; cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py (EXISTS) _send_to_fixme passes write_fixme=False
decisions.step: unlisted: implement the fixme write in transitions.emit

decisions.text: EXISTS (measured 2026-10-30, committed 0a63c4e8 and 851aff51): the falsifier's proof is cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_hand_kick_back_writes_the_fixme_list.py (PROVES 44cc43080f93 all); the tooth test_a_refused_boat_has_its_fixme_list_WRITTEN_ONCE EXISTS in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py and measures cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py; both ran green twice and the hollow reading measured 0 hollow over cairn/tools/base/transitions.py and cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py
